chunks: And from him, from Fadala, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When a free man divorces his slave-girl, and she completes part of her waiting period from him, and then she is manumitted, then indeed she completes the waiting period of a slave-girl.

key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمَمْلُوكَةِ: The waiting period of a slave-girl

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a slave-girl who is divorced and then freed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of continuity in legal status, ruling that a slave-girl divorced by her free master retains her original 'iddah' period (two menstrual cycles) even after manumission, provided the divorce occurred while she was still enslaved. This prevents the legal ambiguity of switching to the free woman's three-month waiting period, ensuring consistency in the transaction of divorce. It highlights the Shia juristic focus on the specific conditions of the divorce act rather than the final status of the woman.
